entities.summary: Manés de Guzmán, OP, was a Castilian Dominican priest who played a pivotal role in the reforming of the Order of Preachers, a Dominican order he helped his younger brother Domingo de Guzmán found. Born in the 12th century, Manés de Guzmán was raised in the shadow of the Reconquista, a period of Christian reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula from Muslim rule. He entered the Dominican order at the age of 25 and rose to prominence as a preacher and reformer, advocating for a return to the order's original mission of preaching the Gospel and caring for the poor. Manés de Guzmán's legacy can be seen in the continued reforming efforts of the Dominican order, which he helped shape into the powerful institution it remains today. Despite his significant contributions, little is known about his personal life, and his death in 1237 at the age of 56 remains somewhat of a mystery.

entities.summary: Manés de Guzmán, OP, was a Castilian Dominican priest who played a pivotal role in the reform of the Order of Preachers from 1221 to 1237. During this period, he worked closely with his brother Domingo de Guzmán, who founded the Order in 1216. Manés de Guzmán's efforts helped establish the Order as a major force in European religious life, with a focus on preaching and evangelization. His contributions had a lasting impact on the development of the Dominican Order, which continued to shape Catholicism and Western civilization for centuries to come. The exact date of Manés de Guzmán's death is unknown, but he was beatified by the Catholic Church in 1237. His legacy as a key figure in the history of the Dominican Order has endured for centuries, with his name becoming synonymous with the order's founding principles. The Dominican Order's emphasis on preaching, evangelization, and social justice has had a profound impact on Western society, and Manés de Guzmán's contributions to this legacy cannot be overstated.
